controversies.title: Accepted donations from real estate developers with active state contracts
controversies.description: Reporting by ProPublica and the New York Times documented that Governor Hochul received millions in campaign contributions from real estate developers, including executives affiliated with Related Companies and Vornado Realty Trust, while those firms stood to benefit from a major Penn Station redevelopment project backed by her administration. After the reporting drew scrutiny, Hochul canceled the Penn Station project in September 2022.
controversies.candidate_response: The Governor stated she canceled the Penn Station project to pursue a more comprehensive approach to transit and development in the area.

controversies.title: Accepted $72,500 in prohibited donations from gubernatorial appointees
controversies.description: New York State law prohibits individuals appointed by the governor from donating to her campaign. An investigation found that Hochul's campaign accepted approximately $72,500 in contributions from gubernatorial appointees, in violation of state election law. The campaign subsequently returned the funds after the violations were identified.
controversies.source_name: New York State Board of Elections / Gothamist
controversies.candidate_response: The Hochul campaign stated that the contributions were returned promptly upon discovery and that the campaign takes compliance with election law seriously.

controversies.title: Found by AG investigation to have sexually harassed multiple state employees
controversies.description: An investigation by the New York Attorney General's office, led by investigators retained by AG Letitia James, concluded that Governor Cuomo sexually harassed 11 women, including current and former state employees, in violation of state and federal law. The report documented a pattern of unwanted touching, inappropriate comments, and a hostile work environment. Cuomo resigned from office in August 2021 before he could be impeached.
controversies.candidate_response: Cuomo denied the findings and stated he never touched anyone inappropriately or made inappropriate advances.

controversies.title: Administration withheld COVID-19 nursing home death data from state legislature
controversies.description: New York Attorney General Letitia James released a report finding that the Cuomo administration had significantly undercounted COVID-19 nursing home deaths, reporting deaths only when they occurred at the facility rather than counting residents who died after being transferred to hospitals. The administration's own internal documents, later obtained by the AP, showed top officials acknowledged the undercount and delayed releasing the full data. A subsequent state assembly investigation found the administration withheld data in response to federal DOJ inquiries.
controversies.candidate_response: Cuomo denied deliberately withholding data and attributed the discrepancy to differing counting methodologies.
